title: The Boy and the Snails
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Farmer's Boy went looking for Snails, and, when he had picked up both his hands full, he set about making a fire at which to roast them; for he meant to eat them. When it got well alight and the Snails began to feel the heat, they gradually withdrew more and more into their shells with the hissing noise they always make when they do so. When the Boy heard it, he said, "You abandoned creatures, how can you find heart to whistle when your houses are burning?"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Boy looking for at the start?
options: Firewood
Berries
Snails
A lost sheep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Boy build a fire?
options: To roast the Snails, since he means to eat them
To keep himself warm in the cold
To signal to his father in the fields
To scare away birds from the crop

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Snails do as they feel the heat?
options: They crawl quickly away from the fire
They stop making any sound at all
They cling tightly to one another
They withdraw more and more into their shells

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what noise do the Snails make as they withdraw?
options: A soft clicking noise
A hissing noise
A low humming noise
A sharp cracking noise

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Boy call the Snails when he hears the noise?
options: "Foolish creatures"
"Frightened creatures"
"Abandoned creatures"
"Stubborn creatures"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Boy mistake the hissing sound for?
options: A cheerful whistling, as if the Snails were untroubled
A cry for help from the Snails
A warning that the fire is too hot
A sign that the Snails are already dead

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Boy call the Snails' shells their "houses"?
options: The Snails have built their shells recently out of mud
The shells were given to the Snails by the Boy himself
The Snails only enter their shells when it rains
The shells are the shelter each Snail withdraws into, much like a home

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Snails "withdrew" into their shells?
options: They pushed themselves out and forward
They pulled themselves back and inward
They rolled over onto their backs
They split open along one side

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "alight" mean in "when it got well alight"?
options: Extinguished completely
Smoking heavily
Burning steadily
Freshly built

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A sound of distress can be mistaken for cheerfulness by someone careless
Snails are more dangerous to cook than most other creatures
Farmers' boys should never build fires outdoors
Every creature deserves to be treated with equal kindness

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many Snails had the Boy picked up?
options: Only a single small snail
A whole basketful of snails
As many as he could carry in a sack
Enough to fill both his hands

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Boy intend to do with the Snails once roasted?
options: Sell them at market
Eat them
Feed them to his dog
Give them to his sister

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when do the Snails begin making the hissing noise?
options: Before the Boy has even lit the fire
Only after the fire has gone out
As they begin to feel the heat of the fire
As soon as the Boy first picks them up

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is actually happening to the Snails as the Boy hears their "whistling"?
options: They are suffering in the fire that the Boy himself has lit
They are singing happily inside their shells
They are calling out to other snails nearby
They are trying to warn the Boy of danger

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Boy's remark reveal about his understanding of the Snails' situation?
options: He fully understands their pain but does not care
He believes the Snails are actually enjoying the fire
He thinks the hissing means they want to be freed
He fails to see that he himself is the cause of their suffering

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does the Boy mean by asking how the Snails "find heart" to whistle?
options: How they manage to breathe inside their shells
How they manage to seem cheerful under the circumstances
How they manage to move at all without legs
How they manage to survive without water

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Boy rescues Snails from a wildfire in the field
A Boy releases his Snails after hearing them hiss
A Boy roasts Snails over a fire and misreads their hissing as cheerful whistling
A Boy trades his Snails for firewood with another farmer
